title: [v0.4.x] Architecture: align service contracts and provider catalog
author: mcpdev80
body:
## Goal

Complete the standards-first service/provider contract alignment before the v0.5.x freeze without discarding working v0.4 capability/provider architecture.

This issue is the single architecture/freeze prerequisite for standards alignment. Existing feature issues remain responsible for their service/provider implementation.

## Architecture rule

> Standards First: BaseHarbor MUST prefer established open standards over proprietary contracts. De-facto standards and established ecosystem conventions SHOULD be used where formal standards do not exist. BaseHarbor-specific contracts MUST only define semantics that cannot reasonably be represented by an existing standard. Extensions MUST remain clearly separated, versioned and provider-neutral.

Every new service kind/provider documents before implementation:

- Existing Standards
- Adopted Standards
- Deviations
- BaseHarbor Extensions
- Compatibility Impact

## Standards baseline

- JSON Schema 2020-12 — portable service/provider configuration schemas.
- Service Binding Specification 1.1 — well-known service connection output names.
- Crossplane — provider/resource/reconciliation architecture pattern only.
- Open Service Broker API — catalog/plan/provision/bind/unbind/deprovision/async lifecycle concepts where useful.
- OCI Image/Distribution — provider artifacts and digest-first registry distribution.
- OpenTelemetry/OTLP — telemetry data plane.
- OpenID Connect/OAuth — identity baseline.
- AsyncAPI + CloudEvents — messaging API/event contracts where applicable.
- RESP — Redis/Valkey-compatible cache and key-value protocol realization where applicable.
- S3 API — de-facto object-storage protocol capability, not generic service identity.

## Required model

```text
application intent
  -> service contract
  -> protocol / semantic requirements
  -> provider resolution
  -> provider implementation
  -> product / engine realization
```

Version axes remain independent:

1. BaseHarbor service contract version
2. provider protocol version
3. provider implementation version
4. product/engine version
5. artifact digest/identity

## Scope

- [ ] Freeze provider-neutral service families: sql, key-value database, document database, cache, object-storage, secrets, messaging, vector, observability, identity.
- [ ] Keep existing v0.4 capability IDs compatible until an explicit migration is tested.
- [ ] Classify existing capability specs as service contract, protocol/semantic capability, or compatibility alias.
- [ ] Make JSON Schema 2020-12 the canonical machine-readable service schema layer.
- [ ] Align service connection outputs with Service Binding 1.1 well-known names:
  `type`, `provider`, `host`, `port`, `uri`, `username`, `password`, `certificates`, `private-key`.
- [ ] Keep BaseHarbor security/lifecycle extensions separate and versioned.
- [ ] Define Runtime Provider Registry vs Provider Catalog as separate concepts.
- [ ] Freeze Provider Catalog descriptor metadata: provider id/version, service kinds, supported contracts/capabilities, product support, platforms, OCI artifact/digest, schema, signature/provenance references.
- [ ] Confirm OCI distribution remains registry-neutral and digest-first.
- [ ] Confirm observability uses OpenTelemetry/OTLP rather than a parallel Baha telemetry protocol.
- [ ] Confirm identity uses OIDC/OAuth rather than a Baha login/token protocol.
- [ ] Confirm messaging adopts AsyncAPI/CloudEvents before implementation (#516).
- [ ] Confirm `database.key-value/v1` remains semantically distinct from `cache.key-value/v1`, with Valkey as reference provider (#516).
- [ ] Confirm `database.document/v1` remains provider-neutral, with MongoDB as reference provider (#516).
- [ ] Confirm vector defines only demonstrated common semantics because no accepted neutral vector-service standard exists.
- [ ] Document compatibility/migration for `object-storage.s3/v1`, `telemetry.otlp/v1`, metrics/logs/traces and other affected existing specs.
- [ ] Conformance/provider SDK checks standards adoption and extension boundaries.

## Keep

Do not replace working primitives that already fit the target:

- provider-neutral application intent;
- capability -> provider -> placement;
- desired/observed/reconcile/verify;
- Provider Integration Contract;
- gRPC/Protocol Buffers external process boundary;
- OCI distribution;
- provider conformance;
- runtime provider registry ownership/placement;
- independent provider implementation version;
- OTLP workload integration.

## Explicit non-goals

- no provider marketplace/server;
- no one-repository-per-provider split before contract freeze;
- no dynamic provider loader solely for this issue;
- no Kubernetes-specific application fields;
- no mass rename of existing capability IDs without compatibility evidence;
- no product versions in generic service contracts.

## Pre-v0.5 acceptance

- [ ] Development Guidelines contain the permanent Standards First rule.
- [ ] Canonical service/provider/binding schemas are JSON Schema 2020-12.
- [ ] Service Binding well-known output names are enforced/documented.
- [ ] Existing contract migrations are explicit and backwards-compatible where promised.
- [ ] Provider Catalog and Runtime Provider Registry are not conflated.
- [ ] #210, #363, #516, #170 and v0.5 freeze/compatibility issues reference this architecture.
- [ ] Exact-head unit/spec/document validation is green before merge.
- [ ] Docker/Podman acceptance only runs if executable runtime behavior changed.

Parent roadmap: #155

Blocks the relevant contract freeze work in #175/#298/#300.


## Runtime/platform standards-first extension

Runtime/platform integration is covered by the same Standards First rule and is implemented in #396.

Before the runtime-provider boundary is frozen, BaseHarbor must audit and classify at least:

- OCI Image Specification;
- OCI Distribution Specification;
- OCI Runtime Specification;
- Compose Specification;
- Kubernetes API;
- CRI;
- CNI;
- CSI;
- Kubernetes Gateway API;
- Service Binding Specification;
- Crossplane provider/resource/reconciliation patterns.

For each area record Existing Standards, Adopted Standards, Deviations, BaseHarbor Extensions and Compatibility Impact.

Only semantics not reasonably covered by an adopted standard may become BaseHarbor-specific runtime-provider semantics.

#396 is the implementation/refactor issue for applying this rule to the runtime boundary. It must complete before the v0.5 contract freeze in #175.
